import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 920

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/166](https://www.erdosproblems.com/166)
- [erdosproblems.com/920](https://www.erdosproblems.com/920)
- [erdosproblems.com/986](https://www.erdosproblems.com/986)
- [erdosproblems.com/1104](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1104)
- [Br26] D. Brada\v{c}, Nearly tight exponents for off-diagonal Ramsey numbers. arXiv:2605.28793
  (2026).
- [Er69b] Erdős, P., Problems and results in chromatic graph theory. Proof Techniques in Graph
  Theory (Proc. Second Ann Arbor Graph Theory Conf., Ann Arbor, Mich., 1968) (1969), 27-35.
- [GrYa68] Graver, Jack E. and Yackel, James, Some graph theoretic results associated with Ramsey's
  theorem. J. Combinatorial Theory (1968), 125--175.
- [MaVe23] Mattheus, S. and Verstraete, J., The asymptotics of $r(4,t)$. arXiv:2306.04007 (2023).
-/

open Real Filter

namespace Erdos920

/--
$f_k(n)$ is the maximum possible chromatic number of a graph with $n$ vertices
which contains no $K_k$.
-/
noncomputable def f (k n : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  sSup {(G.chromaticNumber) | (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) (_ : G.CliqueFree k)}

/--
Is it true that, for $k\geq 4$, $f_k(n) \gg \frac{n^{1-\frac{1}{k-1}}}{(\log n)^{c_k}}$ for some
constant $c_k>0$?

This problem follows immediately from Mattheus and Verstraete's lower bound [MaVe23] for k = 4 and
Bradač's lower bound [Br26] for k ≥ 5.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_920 :
    answer(True) ↔ ∀ k : ℕ, k ≥ 4 → ∃ c > 0,
      (fun n ↦ f k n) ≫ (fun n ↦ (n : ℝ) ^ (1 - 1 / ((k : ℝ) - 1)) / (log n) ^ c) := by
  sorry

/--
Graver and Yackel [GrYa68] proved that
$f_k(n) \ll \left(n\frac{\log\log n}{\log n}\right)^{1-\frac{1}{k-1}}.$
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_920.variants.upper_bound (k : ℕ) (hk : k ≥ 3) :
    (fun n ↦ f k n) ≪ (fun n ↦ ((n : ℝ) * log (log n) / log n) ^ (1 - 1 / ((k : ℝ) - 1))) := by
  sorry

/--
It is known that $f_3(n)\asymp (n/\log n)^{1/2}$ (see [erdosproblems.com/1104]).
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_920.variants.k_eq_3 :
    (fun n ↦ (f 3 n : ℝ)) =Θ[atTop] (fun n ↦ ((n : ℝ) / log n) ^ (1 / 2 : ℝ)) := by
  sorry

/--
The lower bound $R(4,m) \gg m^3/(\log m)^4$ of Mattheus and Verstraete [MaVe23]
(see [erdosproblems.com/166]) implies $f_4(n) \gg \frac{n^{2/3}}{(\log n)^{4/3}}$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_920.variants.lower_bound_k_eq_4 :
    (fun n ↦ f 4 n) ≫ (fun n ↦ (n : ℝ) ^ (2 / 3 : ℝ) / (log n) ^ (4 / 3 : ℝ)) := by
  sorry

/--
A positive answer to this question for all $k\geq 5$ follows from the lower bound in
[erdosproblems.com/986] given by Bradač [Br26].
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_920.variants.lower_bound_k_ge_5 (k : ℕ) (hk : k ≥ 3) :
    ∃ c > 0, (fun n ↦ f k n) ≫ (fun (n : ℕ) ↦
    (n : ℝ) ^ (1 - 2 / ((k : ℝ) + 1)) / (log n) ^ c) := by
  sorry

end Erdos920

findings.description: The variant presented as the positive answer supplied by Bradač uses the exponent `1 - 2 / ((k : ℝ) + 1)` instead of `1 - 1 / ((k : ℝ) - 1)`. At k = 5, it asserts only a lower bound of the form n^(2/3)/(log n)^c, whereas the cited positive answer requires n^(3/4)/(log n)^c. This is a strictly weaker, older bound, not an equivalent formulation obtained by adjusting c. In scratch Lean, the test sequence n^(2/3) satisfies the weaker bound but satisfies none of the stronger bounds, even allowing arbitrary positive real c: n^(1/12) dominates every fixed logarithmic power. The main theorem already has the correct exponent; this defect is confined to the variant.
findings.source_evidence: https://www.erdosproblems.com/latex/920 asks for f_k(n) ≫ n^(1−1/(k−1))/(log n)^(c_k), and states: “A positive answer to this question for all k≥5 follows from the lower bound in [986] given by Bradač.” Bradač, arXiv:2605.28793v3, Theorem 1.1, proves r(s,m) ≥ C_s m^(s−1)/(log m)^(2s−4). Using χ(G) ≥ |V(G)|/α(G) gives the required chromatic exponent 1−1/(s−1), not 1−2/(s+1).
findings.suggested_fix: Replace `1 - 2 / ((k : ℝ) + 1)` with `1 - 1 / ((k : ℝ) - 1)`. The existing `k ≥ 3` range can remain: its additional cases are valid known results. The inferred natural-number logarithmic exponent can also remain.

reformulations.difference: The unannotated existential `∃ c > 0` elaborates with `c : ℕ`, whereas the source allows a positive real logarithmic exponent.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: A positive natural exponent is a positive real exponent with the same power. Conversely, given a positive real exponent c, take the positive natural m = ⌈c⌉₊. Eventually log n ≥ 1, so (log n)^m ≥ (log n)^c, and the required lower bound with exponent m is weaker. Thus existence of a positive real exponent is equivalent to existence of a positive natural exponent, separately for every k. Both the general equivalence and the full universally quantified main proposition were proved without using any conjecture theorem in /workspace/review/scratch.lean.

sources_consulted: https://www.erdosproblems.com/920 — read through https://r.jina.ai/https://www.erdosproblems.com/920, including the recorded solved status.
https://www.erdosproblems.com/latex/920 — exact statement, remarks, and references, read through Jina.
https://www.erdosproblems.com/latex/166 — exact statement and Mattheus–Verstraete bound, read through Jina.
D. Bradač, Off-diagonal Ramsey numbers, arXiv:2605.28793v3, introduction and Theorem 1.1. Read https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.28793 and LaTeX downloaded from https://arxiv.org/e-print/2605.28793.

S. Mattheus and J. Verstraete, The asymptotics of r(4,t), arXiv:2306.04007v5, introduction and Theorem 1. Read https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.04007 and LaTeX downloaded from https://arxiv.org/e-print/2306.04007.
P. Erdős, Problems and results in chromatic graph theory (1969), pp. 29–30, especially equations (4) and (7): https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1969-13.pdf.
Crossref bibliographic record for Graver–Yackel, DOI 10.1016/S0021-9800(68)80038-9; metadata only, full text inaccessible.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/teorth/erdosproblems/main/README.md and https://raw.githubusercontent.com/teorth/erdosproblems/main/data/problems.yaml — mathematical status records for 166, 920, 986, and 1104.

Checked-out Mathlib definitions in SimpleGraph/Clique.lean, SimpleGraph/Coloring/Vertex.lean, Order/Lattice/Nat.lean, Analysis/Asymptotics/Defs.lean, and the real logarithm/power files; repository notation in FormalConjecturesForMathlib/Analysis/Asymptotics/Basic.lean and answer machinery in FormalConjecturesUtil/Answer.lean.
review.notes: All six declarations were checked. Scratch Lean compiles cleanly and proves the supremum is an attained maximum for k≥2, its basic bounds and small values, the exponent separation, and the natural/real logarithmic-exponent equivalence; these proofs do not depend on sorryAx. The last variant's extra k=3,4 cases are not a separate defect. Direct access to pages 986 and 1104 and to the full Graver–Yackel paper was unavailable; the relevant claims were checked against the explicit statements on page 920 and the accessible cited primary papers, including Erdős's quotation of Graver–Yackel. Detailed audit notes are in /workspace/review/audit.md. The reviewed file was not modified.

not_demonstrated.reason: The declaration is a valid but strictly weaker Ramsey-theoretic lower bound, not a statement made trivially true or false by a degeneracy. Proving it for Erdos920.f requires substantive graph-theoretic estimates. The earlier test-sequence comparison establishes that the exponents give different growth requirements, but does not prove or refute this exact declaration.

submission.summary: No trivial-proof file was created or retained, and no compilation was performed for this optional step.
submission.gave_up_reason: The sole reported defect does not admit the requested short, honest proof or disproof of the declaration itself. Substituting a surrogate sequence, merely comparing the exponents, or relying on imported sorry-backed problem theorems would not satisfy the demonstration requirements.

submission.summary: Changed the final variant's exponent from `1 - 2 / ((k : ℝ) + 1)` to `1 - 1 / ((k : ℝ) - 1)`, matching the cited positive answer. No other declarations, hypotheses, docstrings, or attributes were changed. The required compile command succeeds with only the expected `declaration uses 'sorry'` warnings.
